title: A factorial bound for the multicolour triangle Ramsey number
statement:
For every integer $n \ge 2$, the $n$-colour triangle Ramsey number $r_n = r(3, 3, \dots, 3)$ — the least $N$ for which every colouring of the edges of the complete graph on $N$ vertices with $n$ colours yields a monochromatic triangle in some colour — satisfies
\[
  r_n \le \lfloor n!\, e \rfloor + 1,
\]
where $e = \exp(1)$ and $\lfloor\,\cdot\,\rfloor$ is the floor function.
hypotheses_covered: n is a natural number with 2 ≤ n
replaced: ($b$) Noting that $r_2 = 6$, use ($a$) to show that $r_n \leq [n! \, e] + 1$.
